hero.subtitle: When a diagnosis, surgery, or treatment goes wrong at an Albany or nearby Alameda County facility, sorting out what happened can feel overwhelming. LawProactive connects you at no cost with an independent attorney who can review your case.

about.title: Albany Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Albany residents rely on a mix of local clinics and larger Alameda County hospital systems for care, and most of the time that care goes as expected. But when a provider's error causes real harm — a missed diagnosis, a surgical mistake, a medication mix-up — the aftermath often means more medical bills, more appointments, and more uncertainty layered onto an already difficult recovery. California law treats these claims differently than a typical injury case: strict notice periods apply, expert medical review is almost always required, and there's a cap on certain damages that adjusts annually. That complexity is exactly why getting the right guidance early matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a cut of any settlement — we simply connect Albany residents with an independent attorney who handles these cases and can explain, in plain terms, whether what happened meets the legal bar for malpractice. There's no cost to ask.

items.title: Deadlines Are Tighter Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice — missing these can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Expert Review Is Usually Non-Negotiable
items.desc: Most California malpractice cases require a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was breached, so having an attorney who knows how to line that up matters.

items.title: Damages Caps Change Every Year
items.desc: The cap on non-economic damages in California rises annually under MICRA, and an attorney familiar with the current figure can help you understand what's realistically at stake in your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but never more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a mandatory 90-day notice to the provider before you can file suit. These deadlines are strict, so it's worth having them reviewed as soon as possible.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law requires showing the provider fell below the accepted standard of care and that this failure caused your harm — not just that the result was disappointing. An independent attorney can help evaluate whether your situation meets that legal standard.

items.question: I live in Albany near the I-80/San Pablo area — does it matter where my treatment happened?
items.answer: What matters most is where the care was provided and which facility or provider was involved, not your home address. Whether your treatment happened at a clinic near Solano Avenue or a hospital elsewhere in Alameda County, LawProactive can still connect you with an attorney who reviews cases tied to Albany-area residents.

items.question: What does it cost to get a case reviewed?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you receive a recovery.
